briefings.title: Building software-first AI for the real world
briefings.tldr: MIPS has finalized its acquisition of Synopsys' ARC portfolio, positioning the combined entity as the world's largest RISC-V IP provider and driving a "software-first" transition toward custom silicon for edge-based physical AI.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
MIPS has finalized its acquisition of Synopsys' ARC portfolio, positioning the combined entity as the world's largest RISC-V IP provider and driving a "software-first" transition toward custom silicon for edge-based physical AI. By lowering development barriers through virtual prototyping and open standards, MIPS aims to scale its business to $1 billion by 2030.

## Market Consolidation & Scaling RISC-V
- **Strategic Acquisition:** MIPS has officially closed the acquisition of the Synopsys ARC portfolio, merging two of the industry's legacy RISC pioneers.
  - The combination pairs ARC’s energy-efficient programmable cores with MIPS' high-performance, multi-threaded architectures.
  - The combined entity is now the single largest RISC-V IP provider and the second-largest compute and AI IP provider globally.
- **CPU Renaissance in AI:** While GPUs dominated the initial wave of AI, CPUs are seeing a resurgence driven by data orchestration demands.
  - Efficiently managing and feeding data into NPUs and GPUs is recognized as a primary bottleneck in edge and physical AI.
  - MIPS is targeting this bottleneck with agentic AI running directly on high-performance CPUs.
- **Broad Market Engagement:** The company's combined technology portfolio is already deployed or under contract with 50% to 55% of top-tier device manufacturers, fabless companies, and captive silicon creators.

## The "Linuxification" of Custom Silicon
- **Democratizing Hardware Design:** MIPS is championing a shift from proprietary, single-architecture vendor lock-in to an open, software-first hardware approach.
  - **The "Open Orchard" Transition:** The industry is transitioning from a "closed garden" of a few massive chipmakers to an "open orchard" of many custom silicon developers.
  - **Lowering Development Barriers:** AI-driven workflows and open RISC-V standards are lowering the historically prohibitive cost of developing custom ASICs.
- **Decline of Catalog Silicon:** The relevance of off-the-shelf "catalog" silicon is diminishing as large players (smartphone manufacturers, hyperscalers) choose to develop proprietary, application-specific chips optimized for their exact workloads.

## Decentralized Intelligence & The "Sense, Think, Act, Communicate" Paradigm
- **Edge-Based Token Processing:** Real-world physical AI requires billions of tokens processed locally, rather than relying on high-latency, centralized data centers.
  - **The Fern Analogy:** Just as an evergreen fern uses a distributed network of leaf sensors to adapt to weather changes without a central brain, physical AI must leverage decentralized, local decision-making.
- **Revising the Silicon Roadmap:** MIPS has structured its development around four core physical AI functions, moving away from legacy definitions of "big vs. small" cores:
  - **Sense:** Optimizing data movement, analog-to-digital domain processing, and in-memory computing.
  - **Think:** Enabling scalable decision-making workloads (classic AI processing) at the edge.
  - **Act:** Minimizing latency between sensing (e.g., cameras) and physical control loops to achieve human-like responsiveness.
  - **Communicate:** Ensuring high-performance underlying connectivity.

## Enablement Tools & Commercial Trajectory
- **Software-First Prototyping:** MIPS introduced **Atlas Explorer**, a virtual prototyping tool that lets developers test proprietary software on MIPS CPU models before silicon is manufactured.
  - This tool protects customer IP by allowing them to run private workloads locally while verifying processing performance.
- **GlobalFoundries Integration:** Partnership with GlobalFoundries allows MIPS to quickly manifest reference designs into physical silicon, spanning advanced microcontrollers, ASSPs, and AI accelerators.
- **Proven Startup Success:** MIPS validated its lower-barrier design flow with Silicon Valley startup **Apex** (comprising ex-Tesla and ex-Apple engineers).
  - Using Atlas Explorer, Apex successfully migrated its physical AI acceleration algorithm from a costly FPGA setup to a custom ASIC with a small engineering team.
- **Financial Growth Target:** Utilizing a business model spanning IP licensing, software tool subscriptions, and custom silicon capabilities, MIPS target revenues of $1 billion by 2030.

## Notable Quotes
> "Between what we are seeing geopolitically from a regionalization perspective, between what we're seeing from an AI physical AI coming, we predict there is going to be a significantly larger number of silicon developers out there compared to what it has been. It's been a closed garden of a few. I think it's going to be an open orchard of many." - Sameer Wasson on the democratization of custom silicon.

> "We believe Linuxification of hardware is going to do something very similar [to Linux software]. While the cost of doing advanced node silicon devices is going up, we're also seeing the cost of developing silicon is going down because of AI." - Sameer Wasson on how open standards and AI tools are reducing silicon development costs.

> "If we can create systems where the latency between camera and control is deterministic and small, these systems are going to look more human-like. They will be more intelligent. They will be able to react better." - Sameer Wasson on the "Act" pillar of physical AI.

briefings.title: Extreme Co-Design: Building the AI Factory
briefings.tldr: To sustain the exponential growth of agentic AI amid the decline of physical scaling laws, data centers must be re-engineered into highly optimized "AI factories" using an extreme co-design approach across energy, chips, systems, models, and software.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
To sustain the exponential growth of agentic AI amid the decline of physical scaling laws, data centers must be re-engineered into highly optimized "AI factories" using an extreme co-design approach across energy, chips, systems, models, and software. 

## The Macro Shifts: Accelerated Computing and the Rise of AI Factories
- **The End of Physical Scaling:** While Moore's Law technically survives in transistor counts, Dennard scaling (achieving more transistors at the same power and cost) ended in 2005, forcing a permanent shift to GPU-accelerated parallel architectures.
- **The AI Factory Paradigm:** Data centers are transitioning from traditional cost centers running IT workloads to token-revenue generators ("AI factories") optimized entirely for token production per dollar and watt.
- **Exponential Token Demand:** Large language model parameters are growing 10x annually. The rise of "mixture of expert" models and agentic AI requires "test-time scaling," generating up to 100 times more internal tokens for reasoning to yield a single output token.

## Energy and Power Optimization
- **Spiky Training Workloads:** Unlike flat, highly predictable traditional cloud workloads, AI training acts as a collective operation where tens of thousands of GPUs process and share weights simultaneously, causing severe power demand spikes.
- **DSX Operating System:** NVIDIA’s DSX (including DSX Flex and DSX LPS) acts as the factory power operating system to smooth out energy consumption.
  - **Dynamic Storage:** It stores excess energy during low-demand periods and discharges it during peak training cycles to prevent grid failure.
  - **Capacity Increases:** Implementing DSX allows operators to deploy 40% more GPUs per gigawatt of power, leading to a corresponding 40% increase in token throughput and revenue.

## Chips and Infrastructure Co-Design
- **The Vera-Rubin Platform:** The next-generation Rubin GPU is tightly coupled with the Vera CPU via a high-performance, chip-to-chip cache-coherent link.
- **Physical Limitations of Copper:** Copper cabling is highly efficient and power-free but is now limited to a range of just a few meters at high speeds. 
  - **Thermal Engineering:** To keep GPUs within copper-cabling range, 72 GPUs are packed into a single NVLink rack (NVL72), necessitating a shift to liquid cooling and high-voltage DC busbars (moving from 50V to 400V/800V).
- **Spectrum Co-Packaged Optics (CPO):** Placing optics directly onto the switch silicon package avoids the signal degradation of routing across a PCB, saving tens of megawatts of power per AI factory.
- **Ultra-High Bandwidth Networking:** Node communication is powered by BlueField DPUs and ConnectX SuperNICs at 800 Gb/s, with roadmaps scaling to 1600 Gb/s.

## Agentic AI and Specialized Storage
- **Agentic Loops:** AI is moving toward autonomous "agents" that plan, reason, and use digital tools. This is described as "AI eating its own tail," where AI systems generate prompts and actions for other AIs, bypassing slow human inputs.
- **The Vera CPU Mission:** Vera is specifically optimized to run agentic tools, planning scripts, and CUDA-X libraries rather than acting as a traditional general-purpose host.
- **Dual-Tier Agentic Memory:** AI agents require specialized storage architectures to manage two distinct forms of memory:
  - **CMX (Short-Term Memory):** High-speed storage engineered for KV (key-value) caches during active processing.
  - **STX (Long-Term Memory):** Specialized storage optimized for files, object databases, and vector similarity searches.
  - **Performance Impact:** This co-designed storage framework delivers 5x faster token throughput and 5x better efficiency for agentic workloads.

## Notable Quotes
> "In the past, a data center was something that cost money, that you would run IT applications on. An AI factory generates money. It has to generate tokens very efficiently." - on the business model shift of modern computing.

> "An agent is AI eating its own tail. Instead of humans generating prompts, AI closes the loop and feeds the prompt back to itself." - on the transition to autonomous agentic AI workflows.

> "Moore's Law said we would double the number of transistors at the same power and at the same cost... Dennard scaling ended two decades ago... what we need is to reinvent computing." - on the physical limitations forcing architectural co-design.

briefings.title: Industrial-Grade Physical AI for Robotics
briefings.tldr: ABB Robotics, in partnership with NVIDIA, is launching "RobotStudio Hyperreality" in September to bring 99% accurate physical AI to industrial manufacturing.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
ABB Robotics, in partnership with NVIDIA, is launching "RobotStudio Hyperreality" in September to bring 99% accurate physical AI to industrial manufacturing. This integration of high-fidelity synthetic data and digital twins allows companies to pre-train robotic systems entirely in virtual environments, cutting commissioning times by up to 80% and halving time-to-market.

## The Shift to Adaptive Robotics
* **Limitations of Traditional Automation:** Traditional rule-based automation architectures require rigidly controlled environments, perfect lighting, and strict tolerances to operate.
  * Geographically extended supply chains (e.g., production split across Taiwan, China, Vietnam, India, and North America) and shorter product lifecycles make environmental consistency impossible to maintain.
  * Environmental disruptions, like a single failed factory light or a misplaced box, often cause traditional systems to shut down.
* **Embracing Environmental Variation:** To scale globally, industrial robotics must transition to adaptive, data-driven designs.
  * Robotics are expanding beyond automotive assembly lines into high-mix, low-volume environments like logistics, service robotics, and lab automation.
  * Physical AI enables robots to recognize unpredictable real-world scenarios, adapting their motion paths instantly to changes in their environment.

## The ABB-NVIDIA Partnership & Hyperreality
* **Strategic Collaboration:** Announced in March, the partnership merges ABB's industrial knowledge and "RobotStudio" digital twin technology with NVIDIA’s accelerated compute, Omniverse, and synthetic data capabilities.
* **The 99% Accuracy Breakthrough:** Historically, synthetic data was too inaccurate (roughly 80%) for safe human-robot collaboration, requiring tedious on-site training. 
  * The partnership has achieved a **99% path correlation** between virtual simulations and real-world execution.
  * Robots can now be pre-trained safely in virtual environments before physical hardware or parts are even manufactured.
* **RobotStudio Hyperreality:** Launching in September, this software platform enables concurrent engineering, allowing factory engineers to design and test production lines in parallel with a product's development phase rather than waiting for the final physical prototype.

## The Hyperreality Simulation Workflow
* **The 7-Step Deployment Process:**
  1. **CAD Foundation:** Import the CAD model into the RobotStudio cell simulation.
  2. **High-Fidelity Rendering:** Render the environment in precise detail using NVIDIA Omniverse.
  3. **Virtual Camera Configuration:** Set selectable camera views to display the virtual workpiece.
  4. **Variable Configuration:** Define sizes, materials, and positioning of parts.
  5. **Synthetic Training Data:** Generate randomized synthetic data to train AI models.
  6. **VLM Integration:** Deploy ABB vision-language models to simulate the physical working environment.
  7. **Real-World Execution:** Run ABB's virtual controller to ensure 99% correlation between virtual and physical paths.

## Real-World Impact and Business Metrics
* **Foxconn Assembly Case Study:** ABB and NVIDIA applied this physical AI concept to a Foxconn electronics assembly line handling highly complex, miniature components.
  * **Hardware savings:** High-fidelity synthetic data allowed the system to operate with only 1–2 cameras instead of the traditional 5 cameras.
  * **Resilience:** The system continued running seamlessly even when factory lighting conditions changed dynamically.
* **Quantifiable Business Value:**
  * **Setup and Commissioning:** Reduced by up to 80%, allowing production lines to reach target yield in 1 week instead of the typical 5 to 6 months.
  * **Time-to-Market:** Accelerated by up to 50% via virtual concurrent engineering.
  * **Cost Reductions:** Decreased total costs by up to 40% due to minimized physical prototyping and reduced camera hardware requirements.

## Notable Quotes
> "Being 80 percent accurate isn't good enough. You know, we're talking about people safety here in many instances. And if you're not getting accurate synthetic data, you can't pre-train your robot systems..." - on [synthetic data accuracy]

> "I think if we're going to be able to make productive robotic systems that are globally scalable at an industrial scale, I think we've got to embrace the fact that these conditions are not always controllable, and we need our systems to be adaptive to those variations." - on [embracing environmental variation]

> "You don't start when the product is finished. You start when they start developing the product. And then you can then dynamically update the synthetic version of the product and therefore then set up your production lines..." - on [concurrent engineering and synthetic simulation]

briefings.title: Infineon powering AI from grid to core to physical AI
briefings.tldr: Infineon is addressing the massive energy demands of the AI revolution by delivering power and sensing solutions across the entire value chain—spanning grid infrastructure, ultra-high-density data center cores, and robotic physical AI.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Infineon is addressing the massive energy demands of the AI revolution by delivering power and sensing solutions across the entire value chain—spanning grid infrastructure, ultra-high-density data center cores, and robotic physical AI. Through key innovations in silicon, silicon carbide (SiC), and gallium nitride (GaN), Infineon aims to solve the industry's critical bottleneck: scaling AI sustainably.

## Grid-to-Data-Center Power Infrastructure
- **Solid-State Grid Modernization:** Infineon is working with partners to replace conventional 20-ton transformers with semiconductor-based solid-state transformers.
  - The new solid-state transformers are projected to be 30% lighter with significantly increased energy efficiency.
- **Ultra-Fast Fault Protection:** Solid-state circuit breakers are now actively deploying to protect high-voltage data centers and microgrids.
  - **CoolSiC JFET Technology:** These breakers achieve microsecond-level fault isolation, representing a massive leap from legacy millisecond-level mechanical isolation.
  - Infineon announced an expanded portfolio of JFETs supporting up to 1200V with advanced package technology to scale this deployment.
- **Data Center Rack Power Evolution:** Racks are rapidly transitioning from legacy single-phase designs (below 200–300 kW) to Gen 2 three-phase architectures (500–660 kW), heading toward a "North Star" goal of 1-megawatt racks.
- **Agentic AI CPU Support:** Infineon is partnering with major vendors to support the "miniature revolution" of CPU-centric Agentic AI, which demands highly reliable, scalable power architectures as CPU-to-GPU ratios shift.

## Materials Strategy: Silicon, SiC, and GaN
- **A Three-Technology Approach:** Infineon believes no single material can address the AI bottleneck; optimal efficiency requires a hybrid application of Silicon, Silicon Carbide (SiC), and Gallium Nitride (GaN).
- **Silicon Leadership & OptiMOS 8:** Silicon remains the fundamental backbone for power management.
  - Infineon announced its **OptiMOS 8** portfolio, delivering a 44% improvement in RDS(on) compared to OptiMOS 5.
  - New 18-kilowatt and 30-kilowatt Power Supply Unit (PSU) Power Factor Correction (PFC) systems have been launched utilizing this advanced silicon.
- **Optimized Silicon Carbide (SiC):** Designed specifically for high-frequency, high-power functional blocks. Production is scaling out of Kulim, Malaysia, to ensure cost-effective supply security.
- **Gallium Nitride (GaN) Scaling:** GaN is reaching a tipping point, excelling in high-switching-frequency environments like intermediate bus conversion (from 48V down to 6V).
  - To meet soaring demand, Infineon is scaling up the industry's first **12-inch GaN manufacturing facility** in Villach, Europe, ensuring massive scale and cost-competitiveness.

## Ultra-High-Density Core Power Delivery
- **BBU and IBC Innovation:** High-density power storage and conversion units are scaling rapidly.
  - **Battery Backup Units (BBUs):** New pure-play 24 kW BBU solutions utilizing SiC join the existing portfolio (1.5 kW to 12 kW).
  - **Intermediate Bus Conversion (IBC):** High-voltage 10 kW GaN solutions are achieving power densities of 1.6W/mm².
- **Vertical Power Delivery Roadmap:** Moving beyond 2A/mm² vertical power modules currently in production, Infineon unveiled its ultra-high-density roadmap for GPUs, TPUs, and ASICs:
  - **Slim Vertical Power Module:** A 2.5A/mm², four-phase module featuring an incredibly thin Z-height of less than 3mm.
  - **Dual-Phase Solutions:** Advancing to 3A/mm² (substrate attached).
  - **Embedded Substrate Modules:** Target densities exceeding 4A/mm² for next-generation accelerators.

## Physical AI, Robotics, and Security
- **Humanoid Motor Control & Sensing:** Modern humanoids can feature up to 70 joint actuators, requiring complex motor control, sensing, and power management.
  - Infineon provides specialized **MOTIX** controllers, position/current sensors, and its industry-leading **Aurix** microcontrollers (featuring functional safety) to optimize battery life and miniaturize robotic joints.
- **High-Bandwidth Connectivity:** Utilizing recent acquisitions, Infineon is deploying automotive-grade, low-latency Ethernet solutions into robotics to handle the massive data loads generated by physical AI.
- **Nvidia Security Partnership:** Infineon announced a collaboration with Nvidia to secure physical AI platforms.
  - Infineon's **Optiga** security controllers will integrate with Nvidia’s **Jetson Thor** platform, delivering a quantum-resilient hardware root of trust to protect AI models and cryptographic keys in the field.

## Notable Quotes
> "No AI without power, no AI without partnerships." - on the fundamental constraint of artificial intelligence scaling.

> "They actually had to zoom in from milliseconds to get to the microseconds. And as they zoomed in, this was game-changing." - on the ultra-fast reaction times of CoolSiC JFET solid-state circuit breakers.

> "One technology is not good enough. We need three technologies: SiC, silicon, as well as gallium nitride. This gives us the opportunity to walk into customers and give them the best solution." - on material science diversity.

briefings.title: KIOXIA – Exploring the Critical Role of SSDs in AI
briefings.tldr: As generative AI shifts from training to complex agentic inference, SSDs are evolving from traditional storage devices into critical system-level memory extensions that offer the scalability and cost efficiency required to bypass high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and DRAM bottlenecks.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
As generative AI shifts from training to complex agentic inference, SSDs are evolving from traditional storage devices into critical system-level memory extensions that offer the scalability and cost efficiency required to bypass high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and DRAM bottlenecks. 

## The Shift to AI Inference & Storage Bottlenecks
- **Rapid Storage Demand:** The data center NAND market is projected to grow at a 34% CAGR from 2025 to 2031. However, AI inference workloads are growing much faster at a 56% CAGR, serving as the primary driver of storage demands.
- **The Rise of Agentic AI:** Inference is transitioning from simple, single-prompt models to agentic AI, which requires multi-step reasoning, planning, and tool integration. 
  - This evolution dramatically increases token usage, KV (Key-Value) cache storage, and the need for frequent, large-scale data access via Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
- **The Memory-Cost Dilemma:** While HBM and DRAM deliver extreme speed, they are highly expensive and difficult to scale. SSDs offer the optimal balance of massive capacity, scalability, and cost efficiency needed to handle ballooning AI datasets.

## Architectural Innovations: Context Memory & GPU Direct Storage (GDS)
- **Context Memory Storage:** To support long-context inference, modern architectures are shifting to "warm KV reuse." Utilizing SSDs as a scalable memory layer allows systems to offload and share KV cache across GPUs, reducing redundant compute overhead and lowering latency.
- **GPU Direct Storage (GDS):** Traditionally, data transfers from SSDs to GPUs must pass through the CPU, causing high latency. GDS bypasses the CPU entirely, streaming data directly between SSDs and GPUs. 
  - This architecture enables SSDs to act as an extension of HBM, permitting GPUs to process massive datasets, such as vector databases, much more efficiently.

## Kioxia's Specialized SSD Hardware Portfolio
To address diverse AI workloads, Kioxia has developed a three-pronged hardware strategy:
- **CM Series (Context Memory Storage):** Combines enterprise-class performance with high capacity. It is optimized for storing, sharing, and reusing massive KV caches in long-context inference systems.
- **LC Series (Ultra-High Capacity):** Supports up to 245 terabytes (TB) per drive. Designed to store massive AI datasets and enable high-performance tiering directly above nearline HDDs, optimizing total cost of ownership (TCO).
- **GP Series (GPU-Driven I/O Performance):** Built to overcome HBM capacity constraints. It delivers low-latency data access and over 1 million IOPS per GPU, making it ideal for GDS and real-time inference pipelines.

## Software Innovation & The NVIDIA-Kioxia Collaboration
Hardware alone cannot solve the AI data bottleneck; deep software integration across the ecosystem is required.
- **AiSAQ Software Library:** Kioxia’s open-source, SSD-optimized library for large-scale approximate nearest neighbor vector search. By storing vector data directly on SSDs, AiSAQ removes the constraint of needing massive, expensive DRAM arrays.
- **NVIDIA Integration:** AiSAQ integrates with NVIDIA cuVS (a GPU-accelerated vector search library) and the Milvus open-source vector database to accelerate index building.
  - **Performance Benchmarks:** In a single Milvus server test running 5 billion high-dimensional vectors, the joint solution achieved a 57-millisecond latency and 200 queries per second (QPS) at 90% recall.
  - **Efficiency Improvements:** Using GPU acceleration reduced the index build time from a full month to just 4 days (an 8x improvement), while demonstrating a 7x lower search media cost compared to DiskANN.
  - **Future Roadmap:** The partnership is actively working toward scaling systems to support 100 billion vectors, with the ultimate goal of handling trillion-vector workloads.

## Notable Quotes
> "AI performance depends on data, and data is enabled by storage. NAND flash memory is the foundation, and SSDs turn it into real system performance. That is why SSDs are not just components, but the key enabler of modern AI." — Koichi Fukuda on the changing role of storage in AI

> "The next phase of AI will not be defined by compute alone. It will be defined by how effectively we connect compute to data. Training happens periodically. Inference happens continuously." — Dr. Corey Nolet on the shift from compute-centric to data-centric AI

> "At large scale, memory and storage architecture become just as important as raw performance." — Dr. Corey Nolet on scaling infrastructure economically

briefings.title: Physical AI at Scale: From Simulation to Real-World Robots
briefings.tldr: While physical robotics represents the single largest opportunity for humanity, scaling it requires shifting from specialist models to generalist "world foundation models" trained on synthetic data.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
While physical robotics represents the single largest opportunity for humanity, scaling it requires shifting from specialist models to generalist "world foundation models" trained on synthetic data. NVIDIA is addressing this bottleneck through an open-platform strategy built around three computers (training, simulation, and deployment), open-source foundation models like Cosmos 3, and developer tools like Jetson and Isaac Groot.

## The Robotics Opportunity and the Data Bottleneck
- **The Scale of the Opportunity:** Physical operations account for 80% of global GDP, spanning manufacturing, warehousing, retail, and logistics.
  - While the current annual deployment of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), cobots, and industrial arms is under one million units, the ultimate addressable market is in the billions or tens of billions.
- **The Generalist Transition:** Robotics is currently transitioning from highly narrow, specialist models to generalist models, mirroring the "ChatGPT moment" of 2022.
  - Over the last decade, AI deployments addressed less than 1% of the potential market because they relied on combining fragile, task-specific specialist models.
  - A robust generalist model is required to act as the baseline from which specialized physical applications can be reliably derived.
- **The Data Bottleneck:** Unlike Large Language Models (LLMs) that train on vast repositories of internet text, robotics lacks sufficient real-world physical data.
  - Standard physical data collection methods—such as teleoperation, imitation learning, and YouTube videos—are necessary but insufficient to cover edge cases and ensure real-world safety.
  - **Compute as Data:** To solve the data scarcity issue, developers must generate synthetic data. NVIDIA's core philosophy is that compute capacity functions as a data factory to train robot brains.

## NVIDIA's Three-Computer Architecture and Cosmos 3
- **The Three-Computer Framework:** To scale physical AI safely and cheaply, NVIDIA builds and supports three distinct computing environments:
  - **Computer 1 (Training):** High-performance data centers used to train the primary AI models and brain architectures.
  - **Computer 2 (Simulation):** Virtual environments used to rigorously test robot policies, closing the "sim-to-real" gap before physical deployment.
  - **Computer 3 (Deployment):** The physical, edge-compute hardware embedded directly inside the operating robot.
- **Evolution of AI Modalities:** AI architectures have progressed rapidly from pure language to physical action.
  - 2022: Large Language Models (LLMs)
  - 2023: Visual Language Models (VLMs) and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models
  - 2024–2025: World Foundation Models (WFMs) and World Action Models (WAMs) that understand and predict both robot actions and environmental reactions.
- **NVIDIA Cosmos 3:** Launched as the world's premier open world foundation model.
  - To ensure developers can control their own intellectual property, Cosmos 3 is released with complete datasets, model weights, training scripts, and test scripts.
  - Developers can freely use the platform as a baseline to post-train, customize, and build proprietary specialist applications.

## Fleet Orchestration, Agentic AI, and Continuous Optimization
- **The Challenge of Brownfield Integration:** Deploying robots in existing factories requires integrating modern autonomous machines with legacy equipment (such as 10-to-20-year-old PLCs) and various warehouse operating systems (MES/BES).
  - Human-managed integration of these disparate hardware and software protocols is virtually impossible at scale.
- **Agentic AI Orchestration:** Agentic AI is being utilized to automatically integrate and orchestrate various robotics skills and factory systems.
  - Major Taiwanese manufacturers (including TSMC, Foxconn, Delta Electronics, Pegatron, and Wistron) are already using AI agents to optimize throughput, secondary inspection, safety, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
- **The Continuous Post-Deployment Loop:** Deploying a robot is the beginning, not the end, of its lifecycle. When a physical agent encounters an error, it initiates an automated, closed-loop optimization cycle:
  - **Step 1:** The system identifies the error in the field.
  - **Step 2:** AI generates and automatically annotates synthetic data modeling the failure scenario.
  - **Step 3:** The model is fine-tuned and tested in simulation.
  - **Step 4:** The updated brain is redeployed to the physical robot without requiring humans-in-the-loop.

## Hardware and Development Accelerators: Jetson and Isaac Groot
- **NVIDIA Isaac Groot:** A newly announced reference platform designed specifically for humanoid robotics.
  - Historically, building and deploying a humanoid system took research and commercial organizations six to twelve months due to mechatronics and software integration friction.
  - Isaac Groot provides a pre-integrated reference hardware design (sensing and actuation) and an end-to-end simulation-to-real software workflow, reducing setup time to under a single day.
- **NVIDIA Jetson Platform:** NVIDIA's edge AI and robotics developer ecosystem now supports over 2.5 million developers and 10,000 companies globally.
  - **Agentic-Ready Capabilities:** The latest Jetson release is fully optimized for agentic AI, helping developers significantly decrease development time.
  - **Memory Optimization:** Agents are now utilized to optimize memory capacity and select the most efficient models automatically, removing manual engineering bottlenecks.

## Notable Quotes
> "Robotics, of course, is the single largest opportunity in front of humanity... 80% of the world GDP is in the physical world. However, autonomy, which is what you need to make robotics happen... has not really happened yet." - on the market potential of physical AI

> "Compute is data. Without compute, you can't generate all the data that you need in order to train your brain to be... reasonably accurate to start the job." - on the critical role of synthetic data generation

> "Most people think like AI autonomous robots, once you deploy, the job's done. No. That's actually when the job starts because these robots, these autonomous agents, are going to be operating for 5, 10, 15, 20 years, and they're going to get smarter and smarter." - on the necessity of continuous learning loops

> "At NVIDIA, we do not build robots. But we work with literally every AI company, every robotics company in the world, to help them achieve their objective." - on NVIDIA's role as an open ecosystem platform

briefings.title: The Future of Personalized Universal Assistant
briefings.tldr: The global tech landscape is transitioning from a trillion-dollar internet economy built on search and recommendation engines to a new era of "Large Reasoning Machines" and Agentic AI.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
The global tech landscape is transitioning from a trillion-dollar internet economy built on search and recommendation engines to a new era of "Large Reasoning Machines" and Agentic AI. This evolution, exemplified by Google DeepMind's Project Astra, will replace traditional information retrieval with real-time, multimodal, universal AI assistants that reason like humans.

## The Foundation: Search and Recommendation (1995–2015)
- **The Trillion-Dollar Paradigm:** The modern internet economy—including Google, Apple's App Store, YouTube, and Instagram—is built on search and recommendation architectures.
  - This sector comprises $500 billion to $1 trillion of the global internet industry.
  - **The Missed Software Opportunity:** While the US aggressively commercialized these software breakthroughs, Taiwan and Southeast Asia largely missed out on this 20-year wave of software-driven growth.
- **Core Computational Pillars:** Three foundational ideas drove this era:
  - **Reverse Indexing:** Pioneered at scale by Google using MapReduce (invented by Jeff Dean) to index the entire web offline.
  - **Vector Space Models:** Computing mathematical similarity vectors between users and content items to predict user preferences.
  - **Neural Network Optimization:** Utilizing early Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) liquid-cooled clusters to improve recommendation algorithms more than 1,000-fold.

## The Cognitive Shift: Generative AI & Human Reasoning (2015–2025)
- **Sequential Transduction:** The scientific breakthrough that defines "Generative AI."
  - Mimicking human biology, these networks convert sequential inputs (such as audio, pixels, or text) into sequential outputs token by token.
  - **Multimodal Consolidation:** Instead of utilizing separate models for different tasks, sequential transduction allows a single model to handle translation across 100 languages, summarization, and question-answering simultaneously.
- **Chain-of-Thought Reasoning:** The transition from simple input-output pattern matching to active problem-solving.
  - By inserting step-by-step explanations in training data (similar to teaching a child), models improved their reasoning capabilities by 2x.
  - This advancement shifts the definition of AI from "Large Language Models" to "Large Reasoning Machines."

## The Future: Agentic AI & Universal Assistants
- **Project Astra:** Google DeepMind's research prototype for a universal, context-aware AI assistant running on Gemini 2.0.
  - **Agentic Capabilities:** Astra acts as a proactive agent that follows users through daily life via smartphones or prototype display glasses.
  - **Real-World Multimodal Utilities:** The assistant can recall past physical objects (e.g., retrieving a door code from a past email), interpret physical environments (e.g., explaining washing machine symbol settings through a camera feed), and offer localized, real-time context-specific recommendations.
- **On-Device vs. Cloud:** The next major industry debate and developmental frontier will focus on whether these massive reasoning models should run locally on-device or remain cloud-based.

## Notable Quotes
> "More than 500 billion, probably close to a trillion dollars of the entire internet industry is built on recommendation and search. This is how important these concepts are and they will remain very important going into the future." - Dr. Chi on the foundational internet economy.

> "In my personal opinion we should have started calling it Large Reasoning Machines... because the whole point about AGI is not that it can speak our language, it is that it can reason the way that we reason as humans." - Dr. Chi on renaming Large Language Models (LLMs).

> "If you had realized that by 2015 this was possible in neural networks you should have bought more Google and NVIDIA stock. Did you realize that if you put in a thousand dollars in January 1st of 2015 in NVIDIA it would have risen 460 times?" - Dr. Chi on predicting technological shifts.

briefings.title: The Race to Scale AI Data Centers
briefings.tldr: To support the massive surge in AI data center demand—projected to drive global data center energy consumption past 1,000 TWh by 2030—the industry must transition from component-level sourcing to co-designed, factory-integrated systems while proactively navigating lagging regulatory and technical standards.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
To support the massive surge in AI data center demand—projected to drive global data center energy consumption past 1,000 TWh by 2030—the industry must transition from component-level sourcing to co-designed, factory-integrated systems while proactively navigating lagging regulatory and technical standards.

## The Exponential Demand Curve
* **Unprecedented Power Trajectory:** Global data center power consumption is rising rapidly, driven primarily by AI workloads.
  * Historically, consumption grew moderately from 200 terawatt hours (TWh) in 2010 to 240 TWh in 2020 (a 25% increase).
  * Demand is projected to spike to 600 TWh by 2025 and exceed 1,000 TWh by 2030.
  * **The AI Share:** The AI-specific portion of power demand is projected to jump from 90 TWh in 2025 to over 400 TWh by 2030—a four- to five-fold increase in just five years.
* **Massive Capital Expenditure:** Annual global spend on AI data center infrastructure is projected to reach $1 trillion by 2029.
* **Grid and Supply Bottlenecks:** Power availability on utility grids remains a critical constraint.
  * Operators are increasingly moving toward on-site power generation.
  * Small nuclear reactors (SMRs) are anticipated to be integrated into data center power strategies by 2030.

## The Three Axes of Scaling
* **Scaling Up (Density and Power):** Rack-level power consumption is experiencing exponential growth, requiring radical cooling and power delivery modifications.
  * Three years ago, a standard AI rack consumed 10 to 20 kilowatts (kW).
  * Today's systems (such as the NVIDIA NVL72) consume 150 to 200 kW per rack.
  * Next-generation platforms are targeting up to 1 megawatt (MW) per rack, representing a 50x density increase over a five-year period.
* **Scaling Out (Interconnection):** High density requires re-architecting physical systems around the compute cluster.
  * Operators must redesign busway topologies, power conversion architectures, and cooling loops to minimize latency and maintain coherent, large-scale compute clusters.
* **Replicating Globally (Deployment Speed):** Building rates that once took years are being compressed into months.
  * This rapid globalization has dramatically increased supply chain complexity, creating a surge in unique part numbers (SKUs) and supplier components.

## Critical Technical & Physical Transitions
* **Transition to Higher Voltage DC:** Physics dictates a move away from traditional 48-volt racks.
  * At 150 kW+ per rack, low-voltage currents require impractical amounts of copper.
  * The industry is moving to 400-volt and 800-volt DC systems, with 1,500-volt DC on the horizon. This reduces copper usage and allows operators to move power conversion systems outside the IT rack to free up compute space.
* **Mandatory Liquid Cooling:** Air cooling is hitting its physical limits.
  * Air cooling is only effective up to 50–100 kW per rack; beyond this, liquid cooling is mandatory.
  * Open Compute Project (OCP) flow-rate guidelines have increased from 1 liter per minute per kilowatt (L/min/kW) to 1.5–2 L/min/kW in just two years to keep pace with thermal demands.
* **Shift to Factory Integration:** Increased density has altered rack weights, floor-loading limits, and facility layouts. 
  * Integration and commissioning of power, cooling, and controls must happen in the factory rather than in the field to prevent severe scheduling delays.

## Hidden Risks: Market Fragmentation & Lagging Standards
* **Market Fragmentation:** Multiple sectors are scaling rapidly but using highly customized, non-standardized architectures.
  * Total AI chip power is scaling from 2 gigawatts (GW) to 13 GW in just two years.
  * While hyperscalers comprise the majority of this growth (scaling from 1.5 GW to 8.5 GW), the "other" segments—including sovereign AI, neo-clouds, and enterprise—are growing at a faster rate, scaling 4.5x to 5x (from 0.5 GW to over 2 GW).
* **Lagging Standards and Certifications:** Technical standards are not keeping pace with hardware innovation, creating immense regulatory uncertainty.
  * **Voltage Standards:** UL and IEC certification frameworks for 800V DC systems are still maturing and remain unharmonized.
  * **PUE Inconsistencies:** Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) is calculated differently across regions (e.g., EN in Europe vs. ASHRAE guidelines vs. internal hyperscaler specs), leading to expensive regional design re-work.
  * **Cooling Specs:** Rapidly shifting OCP specs mean cooling designs can become undersized or obsolete before certifications are finalized.

## Notable Quotes
> "We're moving away from data centers being designed as individual components, and we're moving towards developing them as complete systems that can be designed, developed, integrated, and deployed all together." - on system-level design

> "The real constraint isn't the technology or the innovation, it's execution at scale." - on the primary industry bottleneck

> "Standards are no longer just a compliance issue, they're a design variable." - on the impact of lagging regulatory frameworks

briefings.title: Unlocking Growth with Industrial & Physical AI at the Edge
briefings.tldr: Qualcomm is spearheading the transition of physical and industrial AI from the cloud to the operational edge, supported by strategic developer integrations and the launch of the IQ10 robotic reference design for humanoid robotics.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Qualcomm is spearheading the transition of physical and industrial AI from the cloud to the operational edge, supported by strategic developer integrations and the launch of the IQ10 robotic reference design for humanoid robotics. 

## The Shift to Edge and Physical AI
- **The Operational Plane:** Industrial AI is shifting from cloud-based processing to local, edge-based execution to support real-time decisions.
  - Historically, the edge captured data and shipped it to the cloud; the new architecture processes and acts on data locally.
  - Qualcomm's hardware supports a wide power continuum ranging from 2 milliwatts up to 200 kilowatts.
- **Three Core Tiers of Edge AI:**
  - **Human-Facing AI:** Interactive, consumer-facing experiences, such as retail cameras recognizing products and prices instantly.
  - **Instrumented AI:** Continuous sensory measurements and predictive algorithms to anticipate equipment failures or safety hazards.
  - **Physical AI:** Automated machinery, wearables, and robotic systems operating autonomously in real-world environments.

## Developer and Industrial Ecosystem Expansion
- **Democratizing Developer Access:** Qualcomm acquired Arduino in October 2025 to put edge AI hardware directly into the hands of developers and prosumers.
  - Launched the *Arduino Uno Q* and the upcoming *Ventuno Q* platforms, which feature integrated vision AI models for quick prototyping.
  - Developer boards enabling out-of-the-box AMR (Autonomous Mobile Robot) development will be commercially available on Amazon in August 2026.
- **Key Vertical Implementations:**
  - **Energy & Utilities:** Collaborating on edge AI sensors in dry, high-wind regions like San Diego to detect and mitigate catastrophic fire risks.
  - **Oil & Gas:** Deploying edge AI infrastructures in partnership with Aramco (Saudi Arabia), ADNOC (UAE), Schlumberger, Siemens, and Honeywell.
  - **Retail:** Engineering hybrid environments that combine human presence with full automation, allowing stores to run unmanned during off-hours.

## Robotic Cognitive Architecture (Systems 2, 1, and 0)
- **The Tri-System Framework:** To mimic human-like operations, Qualcomm breaks robotic systems into three tiers of processing:
  - **System Two (The Brain):** High-level reasoning, strategic planning, and cognitive evaluation.
  - **System One (The Body):** Action execution, mobility, and spatial navigation.
  - **System Zero (The Reflexes):** The low-latency nervous system designed for instantaneous reaction and motor safety.
- **Decentralized Motor Control:** Qualcomm is designing chipsets that move motor control from the central brain down to individual limbs, joints, and digits to enable human-like dexterity and high-frequency actuation.

## Hardware Innovation & Humanoid Robotics
- **The IQ Product Line:** The company offers a tiered industrial product line including the IQ8, IQ9, and the newly announced IQ10.
- **IQ10 Robotic Reference Design (RRD):** Announced as a turn-key platform built specifically for humanoid robotics development.
  - **AI Performance:** Delivers 700 sparse TOPS of AI processing.
  - **Compute Power:** Equipped with 18 safety-grade CPU cores.
  - **Sensor Density:** Supports up to 40 cameras simultaneously.
  - **Power Efficiency:** Operates at a Thermal Design Power (TDP) of 50W to 120W.
- **Neura Robotics Partnership:** Established a rapid partnership in early 2026 (initiated in January, finalized in March) to showcase Neura's "4NE1" humanoid robot running on the Qualcomm IQ9 platform.

## Notable Quotes
> "As the edge starts to become more intelligent, there will be a completely different change in architecture in terms of where the edge becomes intelligent, what is the type of intelligence that you're deploying, what type of models do you need..." - on the structural migration from cloud to edge AI.

> "Physical AI for us is really we as humans what does it mean for us to be able to wear glasses that allow us to be able to have those glasses tell us what the glasses are seeing." - on the expansive future of wearables and augmented physical awareness.

> "We call this AI coming into the operational plane. And AI coming into the operational plane fundamentally for us who think about hardware, who think about semiconductors, it's about this new cycle of change that is about bringing intelligence into the edge." - on the hardware evolution driving industrial automation.

briefings.title: When One Chip Is No Longer Enough for AI
briefings.tldr: As trillion-parameter models and agentic workflows drive demand for high-speed "premium inference," traditional GPU-only architectures have hit a critical cost and performance bottleneck.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
As trillion-parameter models and agentic workflows drive demand for high-speed "premium inference," traditional GPU-only architectures have hit a critical cost and performance bottleneck. SambaNova's heterogeneous disaggregated architecture resolves this by offloading memory-bound decoding to specialized Reconfigurable Dataflow Units (RDUs) while leaving compute-heavy prefill to GPUs, delivering up to a 3x speedup.

## The Shift to Premium Inference and Compute Starvation
- **The Definition of Premium Inference:** Modern frontier AI requires a combination of massive model size (trillion-parameter scale) and high token generation speeds.
  - Users are no longer forced to choose between slow, highly capable models and fast, low-capability models.
  - Top-tier open-source models, such as DeepSeek V2 and Kimi k1.5, are rapidly crossing the trillion-parameter threshold.
- **The Agentic Paradigm Shift:** AI workloads are transitioning from short-lived chatbots to autonomous, long-horizon agents.
  - Agentic systems plan, write code, self-correct, and run for hours or days rather than minutes.
  - A single long-horizon coding task on OpenAI Codex can require over a day of active runtime, generating nearly 13 million tokens and requiring immense Key-Value (KV) cache context reuse.
- **Extreme Compute Bottlenecks:** Enterprise demand for fast, premium inference heavily outstrips current supply.
  - Anthropic’s annual recurring revenue (ARR) grew from $1 billion in 2023 to $47 billion in May 2024, yet its growth is entirely limited by compute availability.
  - Anthropic's "fast mode" for Claude Opus runs twice as fast but costs six times more than standard mode due to the high operational costs of GPU-bound inference.
  - OpenAI, serving over 800 million weekly active users, is actively securing low-latency partnerships (such as with Cerebras) to bypass traditional GPU decoding limits.

## Disaggregated Inference Architecture (GPU vs. RDU)
- **The Core Architectural Flaw:** GPUs are highly parallel systems optimized for compute-bound tasks like training and prefill (processing input tokens), but they are highly inefficient for decoding (generating tokens), which is a memory-bound task.
- **SambaNova's RDU Solution:** Reconfigurable Dataflow Units (RDUs) are purpose-built to handle memory-bound decoding, freeing up precious GPU capacity.
  - **Three-Tier Memory Architecture:** To run massive models at scale, RDUs keep large model pools in DDR, stream active weights through High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), and keep activations close to compute in local SRAM.
  - **SRAM-Only Bottlenecks:** Competitors like Groq and Cerebras use SRAM-only architectures. While fast, their extremely limited memory capacity forces them to split up decoding phases, making it highly difficult to scale to frontier-class models.
- **Strategies for Disaggregation:**
  - *Full Decode Disaggregation:* Prefill runs on the GPU, and decoding runs entirely on the RDU with a single KV cache handoff. This is SambaNova's primary deployment model.
  - *Speculative Decoding:* Utilizing a small draft model on the RDU to speculate tokens, which are then verified in batches by a larger target model. This is being added to minimize latency in high-context agentic workloads.
  - *FFN-Only Decoding:* Splitting the Feed-Forward Network phase from attention. SambaNova is bypassing this approach, calling it a hardware-constrained workaround used by memory-limited chips rather than an efficient architecture.

## Performance Benchmarks & The VectorCORE Cloud
- **VectorCORE Compute (VC2):** SambaNova—in partnership with Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger, Vista Capital CEO Robert Smith, and Cambium Capital’s Landon Downs—launched VC2, a dedicated cloud designed to host heterogeneous disaggregated inference.
- **Real-World Agentic Performance:** During a live demo run out of the VC2 Los Angeles data center, a 10,000-record data science agent pipeline completed an end-to-end analysis, modeling, and report generation task in 45 seconds.
  - This represented a **2x to 3x speedup** compared to running the exact same agentic workflow on NVIDIA B200 GPUs alone.
- **Execution Resource Allocation:** Metrics from the live run demonstrated how tasks were split to maximize efficiency:
  - **RDUs (Decode Phase):** Processed 56% of the execution time.
  - **CPUs (Agentic logic & orchestrating):** Processed 29% of the execution time.
  - **GPUs (Prefill Phase):** Processed 15% of the execution time.

## Scaling Hardware: SN40 to SN50
- **Spatial Execution:** Unlike GPUs that run inference kernel-by-kernel with high communication overhead between steps, RDUs utilize spatial execution to keep compute and communication moving in parallel across the chip.
- **SambaRack SN50 Specifications:**
  - A single SambaRack SN50 contains 16 RDUs designed for agentic inference.
  - The system scales up to **256 interconnected RDUs** across racks, capable of running models with up to **10 trillion parameters**.
  - **The Ultimate Heterogeneous Stack:** The future of enterprise AI requires combining top-tier GPUs (for prefill), SambaNova SN50 RDUs (for decoding), and Intel Xeon 6 CPUs (for tool calling and logic offloading).

## Notable Quotes
> "The combination of these two things, big models running really fast, is the definition of premium inference. And the battleground that exists now is who can offer that best." — *Anton McGonnell, VP of Product*

> "GPUs are incredible computing machines. They are the best system for training and they are the best system for the prefill stage... The decoding phase of inference is a memory-bound problem. Running decoding in RDUs is a better approach, which is going to free up your GPUs." — *Anton McGonnell, VP of Product*

> "We've moved from simple chatbots to really having agents that don't run for minutes but they run for days. They plan, they write code, they fix themselves autonomously. And the scale underneath this is enormous." — *Kwasi Ankomah, Director of AI Solutions Engineering*
